title: EGY-13 · Practical problems: complaining, negotiating, convincing

blocks.text: EGY-13 · Practical problems: complaining, negotiating, convincing
Lesson overview

In Egyptian practice, almost everything is negotiated: the price of a repair, a deadline for work, a favor. And it negotiates with a precise art, made of courtesy, jokes, insistence and formulas that allow everyone to come out with their heads high. In this unit you learn to file a complaint (with politeness or firmness), to bargain a price, to convince someone and to find a compromise (ḥall wasaṭ). The contexts are those of everyday life: a late plumber, a working deadline, a service that does not work. Nine weeks, in parallel with B2-05, B2-06INT-03, the Test B2.1 and the beginning of B2-07.

rows: 12–13 9 weeks (weeks) 175–183), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian partner, authentic videos of everyday life (Appendix C)
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. lodge a complaint in Egyptian, choosing the tone (courtesy, firm, firm) suitable for the situation;
2. contract a price or service with the typical formulas;
3. convincing someone with arguments, guarantees and a little humor;
4. propose, discuss and accept a compromise;
5. understand an authentic negotiation conversation and summarize its outcome.
Nine-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).

Šarīf works on a project with an Egyptian colleague, Mīna, which is in the Cairo headquarters. The client asked for a new version in two weeks. They're talking on video.

7. Egyptian and fuṣḥā Compare

Note. Here Egyptian and fuṣḥā are very close: change the pronunciation (ʾ for ⁧ق⁩ , g per ⁧ج⁩ ) and the forms of verbs. ḥall wasaṭ, bi-šarṭ, mustaḥīl they feel the same in talk shows and news (EGY-12).
8. Listen to an authentic negotiation

What to choose. Scene series or Egyptian movies set at the market, in a shop, in an office; videos of everyday life in which someone contracted or asked for a service; street interviews on prices. Duration: 2–4 minutes. See Appendix C. The method of negotiation.
1. Who and what. Who's negotiating with who? On what (price, time, favor)?
2. The moves. He listens and marks the moves: first offer, reaction, counterproposal, arguments, conditions.
3. The tone. Where are you courteous, where do I stop, where am I joking? What titles do they use (usṭa, ya ḥaggaya fandim?
4. The outcome. Who gave in on what? Resuming in Egyptian (ittafaʾu ʿala...) and in English.
9. Pronunciation

Surprise contracted. alf gnēh?! · ġāli ʾawi! · ēh from ?!: the voice rises a lot and stretches on the last syllable. It's theater: it's part of the negotiation. The loving formulas. ʿašān ḫāṭri · ʿala ʿēni · ya ḥagga they say with softer and slower voices. The ḫ of ḫāṭri It's light, not scraped.

Respond in transliteration; If you want, add the Arabic spelling. The financial statements 1–5 They're also done by word of mouth.
Exercise 1 · Three steps

For each situation write three sentences of complaint, one per step (courtesy, firm, decided): a) The Internet tech was supposed to come yesterday and he didn't come. · b) They brought you the wrong dish at the restaurant, and you've been waiting for half an hour. · c) You paid for a class and the teacher canceled three classes.
Exercise 2 · Contract

Rebuild a negotiation at the Cairo market for a copper lamp (initial price 900 £, target 600). Write 8–10 alternating lines (you and the seller), with at least: ġāli ʾawi, iʿmil maʿāya wāgib, ēh āḫir kalām?, a counter-proposal, nʾsimha nuṣṣēn, a closing formula. fanūs nuḥās Copper lamp (s).
Exercise 3 · Convince

Convince the tutor (8–10 phrases) to: a) come with you to an exhibition of Egyptian art Saturday morning; b) loan you the car for a day; c) participate in a language tandem every week. Use at least four section strategies 4.

13. Oral production
1. The complaint (session). Role-playing game with the tutor: you are a customer, the tutor is an employee (customer service,
hotel, workshop). Start from the courteous step and climb only if needed; you get a solution and you say it again.
2. The market. Contract with the tutor an object of your choice: the tutor is a hard seller. Objective: at least
30% discount, with humor and courtesy.
3. The compromise. With the tutor: you have to organize a dinner together for eight people, but you have different ideas
on site, day and budget. Find a deal in five minutes and summarize it.
